content.text:
I built the figure as a single D3 file, `index.html`. It renders at 1400 × 900 with no console errors. The answer to the question is yes, but in two groups rather than one: LTS releases look alike and interim releases look alike, and the two groups differ.

- **Development:** every release has a development phase of about 6 months before release.
- **Interim releases:** about 18 months of support up to 12.10, then about 9 months from 13.04 on.
- **LTS releases:** 3–5 years of standard support. ESM stretches that to about 10 years from 12.04 LTS, and the Legacy add-on to about 15 years from 14.04 LTS.

The caption's numbers and version names are all computed from the CSV.

```
REPORT
deliverable: index.html
requirements:
  R1: done - one row per release labelled by version, ordered by release date within each group
  R2: done - x = years relative to own release date (0 = release); axis title states unit
  R3: done - dev/standard/extended server/ESM/legacy bars in distinct colours with legend; missing phases skipped
  R4: done - created = open circle, release = black tick at 0
  R5: done - two facets (LTS above, interim below), LTS labels bold
  R6: done - title plus one-sentence caption computed from data (two templates: interim 18→9 months, LTS 5 y + ESM/Legacy to ~15 y)
assumptions:
  - ESM starts at the later of eol and eol-server (eol-server is only used when it is after eol)
  - Years = 365.2425 days; months in the caption = years × 12, rounded
  - Ordering by release date is kept inside each group (LTS facet, interim facet) rather than interleaved
  - Planned dates (after the browser's current date) are drawn hatched; "today" is computed at render time
  - Interim support switch point = first interim release with under 1 year of standard support
limitations:
  - Interim bars are short next to the 16-year LTS span, so interim detail is compressed (hover tooltips show exact dates)
  - Where the planned portion begins changes with the viewing date
  - The facet title "LTS releases (n = 11)" touches the dashed release line slightly
```
